objectives: Decode taught wh-words such as when, whip, whiz, wham and which.
Recognise wh as an initial grapheme while reading the whole word.
Understand that wh and w often share /w/ in many English accents.
Keep the special word who separate because its pronunciation differs.
concepts: In many English accents, wh is pronounced /w/ in common taught words.
The written grapheme wh can be identified even when its sound matches w.
Accurate decoding uses the whole word, including the vowel and ending.
English has exceptions and accent variation; avoid an absolute rule.

definitions.definition: A letter or group of letters representing a sound.

workedExamples.solution: In many accents, wh represents /w/; blend /w/ /i/ /p/ to read whip.
Read the initial wh as /w/ in common accents, then blend e-n.
A special word: wh is pronounced /h/ in common English.

commonMistakes: Expecting wh and w to sound different in every accent.
Guessing a word from wh without checking the rest.
Applying the common /w/ pronunciation to who.
keyTakeaways: Recognise wh as a two-letter initial grapheme.
